title: Implement Conditional Branching Logic with a 'Decision' Node
description: The ChromaticFlow ETL Canvas currently supports linear data pipelines where data flows from one processing node to the next in a predefined sequence. This task requires enhancing the system to support conditional branching. The agent must introduce a new 'Decision' node type that routes data records to one of two different downstream nodes based on a simple condition evaluated on the data record itself. This feature requires modifications across the data model, configuration parser, processing logic, and visualization layer, making it an excellent test of maintaining context over multiple development sessions.

project_spec.name: ChromaticFlow ETL Canvas
project_spec.description:
ChromaticFlow ETL Canvas is an educational, visually-driven data-pipeline playground written in C that turns ordinary CSV/JSON log streams into living color animations. The application invites students and data hobbyists to "paint" with data by mapping field values to shapes, hues, and motions on a dynamic GTK/Cairo canvas while quietly executing a fully-fledged ETL workflow in the background. Users can schedule either batch imports (e.g., nightly sales files) or connect a live socket/pipe for stream processing; every transformation step emits an event that is picked up by the View layer to update the on-screen visualization in real time, highlighting successes, data-quality warnings, or recovery actions when faults occur. 

Built on a classic Model-View-Controller layout, the Model encapsulates file/stream readers, the in-memory pipeline, and a lightweight SQLite staging store. The Controller orchestrates extraction adapters, transformation filters, and loader sinks, exposing a small command API for scheduling jobs, triggering replays, and toggling creative visualization modes. The View, powered by GTK3 and Cairo, renders a colorful node-graph of the pipeline where each node pulses, morphs, or fades based on throughput and data-quality metrics, providing both functional insight and artistic flair. This separation lets developers extend the Model with new sources (e.g., Avro, Parquet) or swap the View for a headless CLI while retaining the same event-streaming core. 

Beyond basic ETL, ChromaticFlow integrates error-recovery routines (automatic rewind/retry, bad-row quarantine), rule-based data-quality checks (null scans, type drift alerts), and a cron-style scheduler for unattended runs. All of these backend events feed the canvas so anomalies literally "glow red" or "splash" across the screen, reinforcing the creative, exploratory spirit of the project.
dependencies: sqlite3 (staging area for batch loads & checkpoints)
